card.name: Heart-event warnings in triptan and NSAID labels
card.fires_on: Commas in lists of chest, throat, neck and jaw symptoms, and the word "fatal" after "which can be" in the NSAID cardiovascular warning. Seen in warnings about heart attack and stroke.

modes.label: Comma in chest-symptom list
modes.description: The comma between body parts like chest, throat, neck and jaw in warnings about pain or tightness.
modes.example: Sensations of pain, tightness, pressure, and heaviness in the chest, throat<<,>> neck, and jaw: generally not associated

modes.label: "fatal" in NSAID boxed warning
modes.description: The word fatal ending the clause about serious cardiovascular thrombotic events, including heart attack and stroke.
modes.example: drugs (NSAIDs) cause an increased risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic events, including myocardial infarction and stroke, which can be<< fatal>>. This risk may occur early in treatment

card.writes: It pushes the model toward heart-related words such as heart and coronary.
card.plain: It lights up in heart-attack warnings, at the spot where the text is heading toward heart-related terms.
